title: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents
claim: Proposes a language-agent architecture organized around working, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory plus explicit memory actions.
baseline: not_applicable
metric: not_applicable
limitations: It is an organizing framework and survey, not a papai implementation or benchmark.
papai_relevance: Defines role vocabulary while leaving prospective scheduling and concrete lifecycle guarantees to this study.

title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
claim: Introduces segment-level recurrence and relative positional encoding to model dependencies beyond fixed training segments.
baseline: fixed-length Transformers
metric: perplexity and bits per character
limitations: Longer dependency modeling does not provide durable scope, contradiction, retention, or erasure semantics.
papai_relevance: Supports treating long context as a bounded working-memory mechanism rather than a complete memory architecture.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
claim: Frames finite-context management as tiered memory with tool-mediated movement between in-context and external storage.
task_or_dataset: Deep Memory Retrieval and conversational-agent tasks
baseline: fixed-context and retrieval baselines
metric: task-specific accuracy
limitations: Preprint evidence; the public project has evolved beyond the frozen paper and is not pinned here.
papai_relevance: Motivates explicit context budgeting and memory actions without transferring published results.

title: Augmenting Language Models with Long-Term Memory
claim: Proposes a frozen backbone with a decoupled side network that retrieves and reads cached long-form memory.
task_or_dataset: ChapterBreak and memory-augmented in-context learning tasks
baseline: long-context language models described in the paper
metric: task-specific language-modeling and downstream metrics
limitations: Requires learned model components and its reported results are not comparable to papai's deterministic retrieval track.
papai_relevance: Illustrates learned external-memory readers and the boundary between external and parametric memory.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
claim: Stores observations, retrieves memories using recency, importance, and relevance, and synthesizes higher-level reflections.
baseline: ablations described in the paper
metric: human evaluation and behavior/task measures
limitations: Its simulated social environment, model prompts, and human evaluations do not establish retrieval quality or safety for papai.
papai_relevance: Provides primary design evidence for episodic memory, reflection, and derived summaries.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
claim: Uses verbal feedback and self-reflection stored across trials to adapt agent behavior without updating base-model weights.
task_or_dataset: Decision-making, reasoning, and coding tasks described in the paper
baseline: task-specific agent baselines
metric: task success and task-specific scores
limitations: Reflections can be incorrect, task feedback differs from user facts, and the paper does not define multi-tenant erasure semantics.
papai_relevance: Supports a separately labeled reflective/experience layer rather than promoting reflections to trusted facts.

title: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
claim: Proposes dynamically structured notes with contextual attributes, links, and updates to related historical memory representations.
task_or_dataset: Six foundation-model evaluations described in the paper
baseline: memory-system baselines described in the paper
metric: task-specific answer metrics
limitations: Dynamic linking and revision depend on model extraction; published task results and lifecycle guarantees are not reproduced here.
papai_relevance: Informs structured fact/link evolution while highlighting provenance, determinism, and deletion risks.

title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents
claim: Exposes store, retrieve, update, summarize, and discard as policy actions and trains an agent to choose among them.
task_or_dataset: Five long-horizon benchmarks described in the paper
baseline: memory-augmented baselines described in the paper
metric: task performance and memory/context measures
limitations: Learned policy decisions are not deterministic lifecycle enforcement and the artifact availability was not established in this freeze.
papai_relevance: Defines an adaptive-policy research family that remains outside papai's deterministic default comparison.

title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion Outperforms Condorcet and Individual Rank Learning Methods
claim: Introduces reciprocal rank fusion for combining result rankings without directly normalizing heterogeneous retrieval scores.
task_or_dataset: TREC retrieval runs described in the paper
baseline: individual and Condorcet-fused rankers
metric: retrieval effectiveness metrics described in the paper
limitations: The paper predates neural retrieval and does not prescribe scope filters, lifecycle checks, or papai-specific fusion constants.
papai_relevance: Provides a deterministic candidate for fusing lexical and dense result lists.

title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
claim: Builds a tree by recursively clustering and summarizing text chunks, then retrieves across levels of abstraction.
baseline: leaf-only and retrieval baselines described in the paper
metric: task-specific answer metrics
limitations: Summaries are model-derived and experiments mix retrievers/readers; deletion propagation and conversational time are not evaluated.
papai_relevance: Provides a primary pattern for rebuildable hierarchical summaries with leaf evidence.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
claim: Combines an extracted knowledge graph with Personalized PageRank for retrieval over newly indexed documents.
task_or_dataset: Multi-hop question answering tasks described in the paper
baseline: RAG and iterative-retrieval baselines described in the paper
metric: retrieval and answer metrics described in the paper
limitations: Document QA differs from scoped conversational memory; graph extraction, temporal validity, deletion, and entity errors require separate testing.
papai_relevance: Supports bounded graph retrieval as a candidate, not an assumption that a graph store solves lifecycle errors.

title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
claim: Proposes extracting an entity graph, forming communities, generating community summaries, and aggregating them for global corpus questions.
task_or_dataset: Query-focused summarization over large text corpora
baseline: naive RAG described in the paper
metric: LLM-judged comprehensiveness, diversity, and related measures
limitations: Frozen evidence is the v1 preprint; model-heavy indexing and LLM judging do not establish temporal or deletion behavior.
papai_relevance: Defines the GraphRAG family and its global-summary use case for comparison with event-oriented memory.

title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
claim: Proposes a temporally aware knowledge graph that integrates conversational and structured data while retaining historical relationships.
task_or_dataset: Deep Memory Retrieval and LongMemEval evaluations described in the paper
baseline: MemGPT and other implementations described in the paper
metric: task accuracy and latency reported by the authors
limitations: Vendor-authored preprint with unreplicated comparisons; its extraction stack and deployment differ from papai.
papai_relevance: Provides a concrete temporal-graph hypothesis while requiring independent local evaluation and conservative claims.

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
claim: Defines benchmark tasks for information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention.
baseline: commercial assistants and long-context/retrieval designs described in the paper
metric: LLM-judged answer accuracy and task-specific measures
limitations: Uses a reader and judge; results depend on prompts, model versions, history construction, and dataset revision.
papai_relevance: Directly motivates papai's long-range, temporal-conflict, update, and abstention slices.

title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
claim: Introduces LoCoMo, long multi-session conversations and tasks for question answering, event summarization, and multimodal dialogue generation.
baseline: long-context and retrieval designs described in the paper
metric: task-specific answer, summary, and generation measures
limitations: Synthetic agent conversations are human-verified but are not papai traffic; multimodal/generative scores are not component retrieval metrics.
papai_relevance: Useful public long-conversation input, reported separately from the deterministic synthetic corpus.

title: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions
claim: Defines MemoryAgentBench around incremental interactions and competencies including accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, and conflict or forgetting behavior.
baseline: long-context, RAG, and agent-memory systems described in the paper
metric: accuracy, exact match, Recall@5, and judge-based measures by subtask
limitations: Aggregates heterogeneous adapted datasets and metrics; some subtasks require model readers or judges and the repository is unpinned here.
papai_relevance: Broadens papai evaluation beyond static retrieval while requiring per-subtask reporting.

title: MemBench: Towards More Comprehensive Evaluation on the Memory of LLM-based Agents
claim: Defines factual and reflective memory levels, participation and observation settings, and effectiveness, efficiency, and capacity evaluation dimensions.
baseline: memory-agent baselines described in the paper
metric: effectiveness, efficiency, and capacity metrics described in the paper
limitations: Its environments, readers, and memory definitions differ from papai's scoped retrieval contract.
papai_relevance: Provides reflective-memory and resource-evaluation cases for an optional public track.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
claim: Demonstrates a dual-encoder dense passage retriever learned from question-passage examples as an alternative retrieval channel to sparse methods.
task_or_dataset: Open-domain question answering datasets described in the paper
baseline: Lucene BM25 and QA systems described in the paper
metric: top-k passage retrieval accuracy and answer exact match
limitations: Open-domain passages are not temporal multi-tenant memories; trained embeddings and reported scores are not used in the deterministic track.
papai_relevance: Supports dense retrieval as a distinct channel whose metadata and failure repair must be explicit.

title: SQLite FTS5 Extension
claim: Documents SQLite FTS5 full-text indexing, query, ranking, tokenizer, and external-content-table mechanisms.
baseline: not_applicable
metric: not_applicable
limitations: Documentation is not a benchmark and the accessed page is not pinned to a SQLite release in this evidence freeze.
papai_relevance: Shows that local SQLite can provide sparse retrieval primitives while architecture must supply scope and lifecycle semantics.

title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
claim: Studies factual associations in model parameters and proposes rank-one model editing with evaluation of efficacy, generalization, and specificity.
task_or_dataset: CounterFact and zero-shot relation extraction model-editing tasks
baseline: fine-tuning and model-editing baselines described in the paper
metric: efficacy, generalization, specificity, and related editing measures
limitations: Model editing does not provide per-user provenance, access filtering, or reliable hard erasure and is outside papai's default runtime.
papai_relevance: Defines parametric memory and explains why it is not interchangeable with an external auditable store.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
claim: Demonstrates a backdoor attack that poisons similarity-retrieved long-term memory or a RAG knowledge base so triggered queries retrieve malicious demonstrations.
task_or_dataset: AgentDriver, StrategyQA/ReAct, and EHRAgent settings described in the paper
baseline: clean-memory and attack baselines described in the paper
metric: attack success, benign utility, and retrieval-related attack measures
limitations: The threat demonstrations use task-specific agents, embedders, models, and datasets; the repository is unpinned and no attack or defense is reproduced here.
papai_relevance: Motivates treating persistent memory as untrusted data, separating relevance from authority, and testing poison propagation through derived state.

title: How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
claim: Studies memory addition and deletion across several agents and reports error propagation, misaligned experience replay, and benefits from quality-aware memory management in the evaluated settings.
task_or_dataset: Four agent and task settings described in the paper
baseline: fixed memory, add-all, selective-addition, and deletion strategies described in the paper
metric: task performance, memory dynamics, similarity, and resource-constrained results
limitations: The released artifact covers only the AgentDriver patches and setting, depends on separately obtained AgentDriver code and data, and does not provide the paper's other settings; it is unpinned and not reproduced here.
papai_relevance: Supports quality-gated promotion into experience replay while keeping canonical evidence and governance deletion separate.

title: Mem2ActBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Utilization in Task-Oriented Autonomous Agents
claim: Evaluates whether agents apply long-term memory to tool selection and parameter grounding rather than only answer explicit recall questions.
baseline: seven memory frameworks described in the paper
metric: task execution and memory-dependent tool-use measures described in the paper
limitations: The benchmark uses synthesized sessions, model-driven agents, and tool environments; its repository is unpinned and its scores are not component-retrieval scores.
papai_relevance: Motivates a separate downstream action-utilization track for papai without changing the deterministic retrieval score.

title: GroupMemBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent Memory in Multi-Party Conversations
claim: Defines multi-party group-memory cases with speaker-grounded beliefs, threaded dynamics, audience-adapted language, knowledge updates, temporal reasoning, and abstention.
baseline: BM25, dense retrieval, and agent-memory systems described in the preprint
metric: answer accuracy, construction cost, and storage measures described in the preprint
limitations: Preprint evidence with synthetic English enterprise conversations and model-generated evaluation components; the dataset revision and companion code are not pinned here.
papai_relevance: Exposes group and thread semantics that personal/group namespace isolation alone does not evaluate and requires a simple lexical baseline.

title: Beyond a Million Tokens: Benchmarking and Enhancing Long-Term Memory in LLMs
claim: Introduces BEAM with coherent synthetic conversations from 100K to 10M tokens and probes ten long-term-memory abilities, alongside the LIGHT memory architecture.
baseline: long-context, retrieval-augmented, and memory-architecture baselines described in the paper
metric: ability-specific answer measures across conversation-length tiers
limitations: The benchmark is model-reader based, synthetic, expensive at its largest tiers, and distinct from record-count retrieval scaling; code and data are unpinned here.
papai_relevance: Adds a token-horizon scale axis that the existing 100K-record distractor profile does not establish.

title: PM-Bench: Evaluating Prospective Memory in LLM Agents
claim: Evaluates whether agents execute, update, cancel, or withhold deferred intentions at the correct future time or event while continuing ongoing activity.
baseline: single-agent, ledger, heartbeat, and multi-agent configurations described in the paper
metric: set F1, precision, false actions, due-task hits, and monitoring cost
limitations: The benchmark is newly released, model-dependent, and evaluates agent execution rather than retrieval alone; the repository is unpinned here.
papai_relevance: Provides a direct future benchmark for papai prospective memory, including rescheduling, cancellation, false execution, and monitoring overhead.

title: Dissecting GraphRAG: A Modular Analysis of Knowledge Structuring for Factoid Question Answering
claim: Analyzes triple extraction, community granularity, and report generation, finding that extraction quality can bottleneck GraphRAG and that deterministic templates outperform LLM reports in the evaluated QA settings.
baseline: module variants with controlled graph and reporting choices described in the paper
metric: retrieval, answer, extraction-quality, and efficiency measures described in the paper
limitations: Biomedical and encyclopedic factoid QA differ from temporal multi-tenant conversation memory; the implementation and data are unpinned and no result is reproduced here.
papai_relevance: Supports measuring extraction and path quality separately and testing deterministic graph verbalization instead of assuming model summaries help.

title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
claim: Presents a fact-extraction memory and a graph-enhanced variant; the authors report a small overall graph-over-base gain on their LoCoMo evaluation alongside latency and token comparisons.
baseline: memory systems, RAG chunking, full-context, proprietary, and graph/base variants described in the preprint
metric: F1, BLEU-1, LLM-judge, token, and latency measures
limitations: Vendor-authored preprint; its evaluation excludes the unanswerable category, uses model extraction and judging, and the current repository has evolved beyond the paper-era implementation without a pinned commit here.
papai_relevance: Provides hypothesis-generating direct graph-versus-non-graph agent-memory evidence while reinforcing the need for a strict local graph gate.
